findings.reason: The Definition equates K(X,Y)=g(∇_X n,Y) with 1/2 L_n h, but h is defined only on Σ and n is normal, not a vector field on Σ. The cited GR initial-data definition supplies only the covariant-derivative convention. Define the required normal foliation and induced metric family, or remove or qualify this equality.

The SI paragraph gives units but leaves the physical roles and primitive/derived status of G_N, μ_0 and Λ unstated. Identify their roles as model parameters and distinguish them from derived κ; state the intended SI interpretation without implying measured numerical values.

The unit paragraph sets y^i=x^i/L_0 while x^i already denotes a coordinate on T^3_{2π}. Distinguish the dimensionless torus coordinate from a length coordinate, and specify which components of h, K, e and b are represented in the componentwise Sobolev spaces.

Definition (c) and Proof 1.3 use nonnegativity and monotonicity of density integrals and a supremum in the extended reals. The listed suppliers define the integrals and extended-real order, but do not supply those properties or completeness. Cite the exact density-integration and extended-real-completeness results, or prove the needed facts locally.

The Statement claims uniqueness among Sobolev solutions, while Proof 1.2 invokes a supplier whose uniqueness conclusion covers classical solutions only. Add a local argument that every solution in the stated Sobolev class is classical under these hypotheses, then apply the uniqueness result.

The gauge proof needs smooth χ, but the cited local well-posedness statement supplies C^1 existence; add and apply the exact smooth-persistence supplier on the same interval. Also define the scalar operator Box_g χ and specify the lower-order term L used in the first-order system.

The periodic clause applies H^s spaces and curvature operations to tensor fields without specifying their torus components or how vector e,b are obtained from the upstream observer covectors. State the h-raising convention and component types, and define D and R(h) on the regular representatives guaranteed by the Sobolev hypotheses.

Facts F4 and Proof 1.1 use the spatial Hodge star *_h and the identity d(i*F)=i*(dF); neither is stated by the listed suppliers. Define or cite the oriented Riemannian Hodge star and supply the pullback identity or its coordinate proof before deriving the Maxwell divergence constraints.

The Statement evaluates the harmonic-gauge vector defined for a smooth spacetime metric on finite-regularity initial metric data, without assuming or constructing a neighborhood metric. Define its initial-slice value directly from the prescribed 1-jet, or state a regularity-adequate extension and its hypotheses.
